summary: An excerpt from a military fiction novel, Book 15 part 49, following Gunny Ray as his Marine squad is inserted by helicopter into a desert area for an operation. Ray keeps the comm channel open, sees the canyon differs from satellite imagery, and positions his men (Dhamers, Kluge, Hanfland) to cover the entrance and high ground. The passage is tense and tactical, focused on sensory detail and the squad's coordination.
one_line: Gunny Ray leads a Marine squad inserted by helicopter into a desert box canyon on a surprise operation.
key_facts: Ray presses the pickups on his throat against his vocal chords so he doesn't have to shout over the rotor racket.
Ray tells the pilots that the LT says surprise is essential to the operation and to make the hover two klicks out and stay on alert.
The pilot replies 'Whatever you say, Gunny, since the tape's running', a reference to the craft's flight data recorder.
Ray flips his comm to the open channel and informs his men that the drop point is getting fat.
The choppers peel back to a safe recon position after the Marines are on the ground.
The squad sprints almost due east, with profiles low.
Ray drops the visor on his command helmet, and a computer simulation tracks his squad of seven as orange blobs around a yellow sliver representing him.
Ray switches the display from light enhanced night vision to infrared with a sub-vocalized command.
The narrow canyon is a sandblasted gully of tight switchbacks, and its sides are sheer and devoid of footholds, unlike the satellite-generated model.
The canyon is described as one way in, one way out territory, a reduced scale model of a wild west box canyon.
Dhamers plants himself behind an outcropping to cover the entrance with his subby and remote detonated personnel mines.
Kluge deploys right and Hanfland left, up the incline of New Mes bedrock to provide crossfire from the high ground.
